x: Racing over a terrain of pathways, gravel and mud, in icy conditions, Roger Alsop came home 2nd to former world mountain racing champion Martin Jones with 32:08 to 30:09.

…were prominent from the instant the race began but one of the sights to remember over a lifetime of athletics came when Captain Roger Alsop, back from Germany just the night before, burst through only a minute or so into the race to lead the field with the whole Belgrave pack falling in behind him i…
Shaftesbury still led but the Bels were now up to 5th. Captain Roger showed that he is in terrific form and full of confidence by turning in a 13:21 which moved us up to 2nd.

Our own Najibe Hliouat, running more consistently and getting better very time out, worked hard and moved into second but the order changed again on stage three when Boxhill's Paul Hayward not surprisingly got the better of Cap'n Roger, just back from honeymooning in Australia.

With our running Captain Roger Alsop due to marry Helen Maskrey, our Skipper decided to hold his stag celebrations over the weekend of the Surrey Road Relay which became the first event in the most confusing and violently contested multi-event competition that the participants had ever entered into.
